title: The Years Given Back
old_p1: Joel’s land had a hard time. Locusts, bugs like big grasshoppers, came in huge crowds and ate the plants, and the people were hungry. Then Heavenly Father made a happy promise. “Fear not, O land,” He said. “Be glad and rejoice.”
He promised soft green grass on the hills and sweet fruit on the trees again.
old_p2: “I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten,” He said. Restore means give back. There would be plenty of wheat, and they would eat and be full.
He promised more: “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.” All flesh means all people. Long after, Jesus’ friend Peter said this came true when the Holy Ghost came.
Tonight, feel happy and safe. Heavenly Father gives good things back.
p1: The prophet Joel’s land had a hard time. Locusts came in huge crowds. Locusts are bugs like big grasshoppers. They ate the plants, and the people were hungry.
Then Heavenly Father made a happy promise. “Do not be afraid,” He said. “Be glad and rejoice!” Rejoice means to be full of joy.
He promised green grass, fruit on the trees, and rain at just the right time.
p2: He said, “I will give you back the years the locusts have eaten.” There would be plenty of wheat for bread. He also promised to send His Spirit to all people. Later, Peter, Jesus’ friend, said this came true when the Holy Ghost came.
Heavenly Father can bring good things back. Tonight you can feel glad, and thank Him for the food He gives you.
